principles: Authored CANDIDATE is not historical recovery.
A valid curriculum use does not by itself promote language authority or productivity.
A stale rationale or stale phonological annotation creates review debt rather than automatic candidate invalidation.
Dependencies on GATE, WATCH or unresolved assets must remain machine-visible.

disposition_model.KEEP: Candidate survives A1-A7 with no material rationale defect; remains CANDIDATE unless separately promoted.
disposition_model.KEEP_SCOPED: Candidate remains useful only inside its current governed scope; no global productivity.
disposition_model.REVIEW: Candidate may remain registered, but rationale, phonology, semantics or dependency requires re-review.
disposition_model.UNRESOLVED_DEPENDENCY: Candidate materially depends on a GATE/WATCH/unresolved asset or unapproved rule.
disposition_model.RATIONALE_WEAKENED: Candidate may remain as authorship, but the prior corpus-facing derivation lost evidentiary weight.
disposition_model.RETIREMENT_CANDIDATE: Noncanonical proposal should be archived/superseded unless re-justified.

cross_candidate_findings.finding: The authored registry is generally well-governed: all 20 entries are CANDIDATE and deny historical recovery.
AN, EN, KU, KE, ZAMI and KALA are the strongest surviving evidence-mapped candidates, all scoped.
cross_candidate_findings.implication: Course repetition cannot promote them globally.

cross_candidate_findings.finding: KUVAN survives better as a closed authored specialization than as proof of productive KU+VAN morphology.
KUON is the highest dependency-risk registered candidate because ON remains GATE and proposal history conflicts.
VALA is the strongest semantic-rationale debt.
HOYU is the strongest phonological-metadata debt in the authored registry.
A8 justifies no immediate canonical deletion; preserve history via review and supersession.
